Subject: Staged MAP: evaluation & conversion questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile and token-cost breakdown were exactly what our infra team wanted to see. We need to formalize a short Mutual Action Plan so procurement and engineering have clear milestones for the POC -> paid conversion. A few specific asks: 

- Can Redwood confirm how POC credits roll over if we hit partial milestones but not full conversion by the trial end?
- What are the discount tiers for committing to a ramped monthly commit vs a flat annual commit?
- We may need a 30-day extension on the free trial window if the integration work slips — is that possible without re-running security scans?

Procurement asked that we get a simple MAP and SOW they can attach to the purchase request. Appreciate a one-pager we can share that maps deliverables -> acceptance criteria -> credit releases.

Best,
Emma

Head of Integrations
FinTechHQ

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>

Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged MAP: evaluation & conversion questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Drafting a concise MAP and SOW attached (MAP_draft_v2.pdf, SOW_staged_evaluation.docx). Highlights below; happy to hop on a quick call to finalize with procurement.

Proposed Staged MAP (high level):
1) Week 0-3: Integration & smoke tests
   - Deliverable: data plumbing + sample end-to-end eval.
   - Acceptance: < 200ms 95th percentile on sample load; end-to-end signed-off by your infra lead.
   - Credit release: 25k token credits on sign-off.

2) Week 4-6: Feature evaluation (reranking + chat flows)
   - Deliverable: 1 production-like workload test & quality checkpoint with your PM.
   - Acceptance: quality gates for intent accuracy >= baseline; integration report.
   - Credit release: 25k token credits on sign-off.

3) Week 7-12: Scale/ramp + pre-production test
   - Deliverable: throughput run at target QPS and monitoring hooks enabled.
   - Acceptance: agreed throughput + alerting/trace availability.
   - Credit release: remaining 50k token credits on sign-off.

Credit rollover / extension policy (proposal):
- Unused credits at milestone can be rolled forward to the next milestone within the 90-day MAP window.
- If MAP extends beyond 90 days due to integration delays, Redwood will allow a single 30-day trial extension without re-running full security scans (provided the integration scope is unchanged).

Commercials / conversion pricing (early-commit incentives):
- Option A (Q3 ramp commit): 6-month ramp commit starting at 200k tokens/mo rising to 500k tokens/mo — 15% conversion credit applied to first 3 months.
- Option B (Annual commit): 12-month commit at a blended rate — 20% conversion credit and guaranteed pricing cap.
- If FinTechHQ signs an MSA with a committed NPU/throughput tier by 2026-06-15, we can extend a one-time 20% off list for the first year (to recognize the MAP milestones).

Next steps:
- I attached the draft MAP and SOW for your procurement/engineering review.
- If procurement is comfortable, we can push the SOW to DocuSign and lock the trial extension + credit allocation.

Attachments: MAP_draft_v2.pdf (one-pager MAP), SOW_staged_evaluation.docx

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@fintechhq.com>

Cc: FinTechHQ Procurement <procurement@fintechhq.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@fintechhq.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Staged MAP: evaluation & conversion questions

Rishi — this is very helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from procurement/security: 

- Procurement would like the MAP one-pager to include a clear invoice path for the conversion credits (so they can code the request). Can you add a short appendix that maps credit releases to invoice line items?
- Legal flagged the trial extension language; they want assurance that the extension does not change data residency commitments (we are staying in us-east only).
- Can you confirm the DocuSign SOW will include the optional annual commit clause and a placeholder for the signature that procurement can pre-approve?

Assuming we get those items, procurement aims to finalize the PR by 2026-05-20 to meet our monthly finance cutoff. If we can get the DocuSign link and the updated one-pager this week, they can attach it and proceed.

On the credit amounts: the team is comfortable with the staged releases you proposed, but asks whether Redwood can guarantee the final 50k credits won't be reclaimed if we later show a lower-than-expected production token profile — we need confidence that the final milestone is meaningful and not subject to post-hoc adjustment.

Happy to take a 20-minute call Tuesday to walk procurement/legal through the draft.

Best,
Emma
